sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the high Savuto River valley, in the SW boundary of the Sila Massif in central/western Calabria, between the towns of Cosenza (to the north) and Lametia Terme (to the south). This source is a low-angle, SE-dipping, fault located in the southwestern sector of the extensional axis that runs along the southern Apennines.
Historical catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a remarkable concentration of damaging earthquakes in the area. In particular, this region has been struck by the 27 March 1638 (Mw 7.0, Calabria Centrale) event. The overall region was also affected by large earthquakes on 5 November 1659 (Mw 6.5, Calabria Centrale), 5 and 28 February 1783 (both Mw 7.0, Calabria), and 8 September 1905 (Mw ca. 7.0, Calabria).
This source is thought to be the northernmost expression of the ca. E-dipping, large normal fault system that runs along the western seaboard of the Calabria region. These faults make up the extensional Calabrian back-arc system, to the west of the mountain crest. The high Savuto River valley, with its outlet to the southwest in the Tyrrhenian sea, is characterized by an asymmetric transversal trend, slightly steeper on the western side. It is also encircled by regional transverse tectonic lines generally referred to in the literature as "Vette Line", to the north, and "Lamezia-Catanzaro Line", to the south (Italiano et al., 2010). This asymmetric valley is markedly separated from the Crati River valley, just to the north, that outlets northwards, and from the S. Eufemia plain, lying to the south, across the the "Lamezia-Catanzaro Line".
Although the area is poorly investigated from a seismotectonic viewpoint, we propose that this valley can be explained with a low-angle, E-dipping large normal fault, acting as the northern termination of the long extensional fault system that runs along the Calabrian back-arc from the Messina Straits to the north, including the Gioia Tauro plain, the Mesima-Marepotamo valley, and the S. Eufemia plain.
The strike of the source was inferred from morpho-tectonic considerations. The dip, and the rake, indicative of almost pure normal faulting, are inferred from geological considerations and tectonic comparison with other structures of the the E-dipping extensional axis along the Calabrian back-arc. The minimum and maximum depth were inferred from regional geological and seismological considerations. The slip rate was inferred from regional geodynamic constraints data.
